population_note_text: Every voucher in the books population. Party ledgers are those under Sundry Debtors, Sundry Creditors, Loans (Liability) or Loans & Advances (Asset); bank and cash, those under Bank Accounts, Bank OD A/c or Cash-in-Hand.

figures.definition_text: Debits on party ledgers in the vouchers settling one party through another with no bank or cash line, summed -- a candidate total, not a reportable amount.

figures.definition_text: Bank and cash lines of the vouchers whose narration names a party ledger with no amount on the voucher, summed -- a candidate total, not a reportable amount. A Contra, or any voucher whose every line with an amount is on a bank or cash ledger, counts the larger side of its bank and cash lines once.

Bank and cash lines of the vouchers whose narration holds a party's name only inside a longer name, summed -- a candidate total, not a reportable amount. A Contra, or any voucher whose every line with an amount is on a bank or cash ledger, counts the larger side of its bank and cash lines once.
Bank or cash vouchers whose narration holds a party ledger's name only inside a longer name (another name-like word beside it in the same part of the narration); listed apart from the others.
Voucher and named-party pairs across the groups: equal to the voucher count unless a narration names more than one party.
Bank or cash vouchers whose narration names, as whole words, a party ledger with no amount on the voucher.

findings.title_text: Journals settling one party through another, with no bank or cash line: listed for the CA (may bear on clauses 31 and 21(d))
limits_text: Listed, never judged: the candidate total is not a reportable amount, and nothing is left out for being small or looking harmless. Whether a row is a payment under s.40A(3), a Rule 6DD case, a loan or deposit, a trade set-off, or one person under two ledgers is the CA's to determine; no clause 31 or 21(d) row is written.
Recall is not measured on real books.
Same-person set-offs, rectifications of a wrong-party posting, opening or migration entries, branch ledgers of one entity, and discount or note journals against one party are listed too.
ask_client_text: Journal settling one party through another: whose liability, and who received the value? Is it a loan or deposit taken or repaid by journal (clause 31, codes I/J), a same-person set-off, or a correction?
